pages.title: System of Transliteration Adopted

observations: Part A describes a curved/tilde upper mark over a nasalized letter for Anunasika/Chandra-bindu. Part B repeats an upper nasalization sign for nun ghunna. This supports an available nasalization convention but does not identify every damaged Kui mark.

Part C explicitly reserves special language-specific letters for the relevant language sections. A general Sanskrit/Arabic transliteration value must not override the Kui chapter or the quoted Smith witness.

Part D distinguishes additional phonetic vowel symbols; it also identifies an apostrophe as the notation for Munda semi-consonants. Neither statement warrants reinterpretation of Kui punctuation without local evidence.
Part E uses acute accents to mark an accented syllable. A straight/slanted nasal-consonant upper mark in specimen40 cannot therefore be silently interpreted as stress or changed to a vowel accent.

The key distinguishes omitted vowels from raised small characters for silent or weakly pronounced medial/final vowels. Any raised characters encountered must be recorded as printed rather than silently flattened or deleted.
decisions: Keep curved upper-i marks provisionally encoded with tilde when supported by the individual image, preserving source-mark-encoding uncertainty until chapter and repeated-glyph review settle them.
Do not resolve the marked consonant in the to-see paradigm by importing the general visarga value of dotted h. The image-only meḥpa proposal remains distinct from a phonological interpretation.
Preserve specimen-specific mark-shape observations for Smith40 rather than harmonizing all nasal marks to the other specimens.
